label: Muted Trumpet, sampled, close and dry
audition_title: libsonare muted trumpet vs the sampled reference
_notes: Every fourth semitone from 54 to 76, which is exactly the grid the open trumpet on the neighbouring slot was captured against. That is the point of it: the two are the same instrument with and without a mute, so measured on one grid they can be read against each other cell for cell, and what the mute does is the difference between them.
_velocities: Five, matching the slots of this rack captured earlier so that one axis covers the whole of it. The axis is live here at 12.8 dB between velocity 16 and 104.
_dry: Nothing to switch off, measured rather than assumed: with the rack loaded not one of the plugin's 1526 advertised parameters matches `reverb` or `delay`, so `dry` has no section to act on and is left off rather than claiming an effect was disabled. What the recording contains is answered by `room`, which is a different question.
_room: No room, and the answer has to be declared because no note-tail measurement can reach it: a release and a small hall are the same falling signal over the tail a capture records, and the per-note agreement test that separates a room from one note's decay passes on a release perfectly. `calibrate` measures RT60 0.00 s. With the rack loaded, not one of the 1526 parameters the plugin advertises matches `reverb`, `delay` or `room`, and every slot of it captured in an earlier round recorded no space.
_stimulus: Three seconds, the family's. This voice sustains rather than decaying, so the gate is the length of the measurement rather than a window over an event: it is still sounding 2.9 dB under its peak when the key lifts, which is what makes `damper` measurable here and what the previous reading of this slot said was impossible.
_calibration: From `capture.py calibrate` on this rack, whose settings this capture adopts from the slots of it captured earlier so they stay comparable: a two-second settle against a measured minimum of 250 ms, and two renders of one cell bit-identical, so there is no round robin to put a floor under the loss. `realtime` is kept on although the reference renders the same either way, because a note streamed late is caught only by `verify` and would otherwise be committed as a measurement.
_timbres: One, and the ladder is monotone above it, so this capture cannot move the voice past `voiced` however complete its coverage. That is a property of the source rather than of the work: the rack holds one slot per GM program, so there is no second muted trumpet in it to disagree with, and `source_for` takes every timbre of a capture from one plugin. What the reference does buy is the thing there was none of before -- a measured target for `autofit` and `--diagnose`, in place of voicing this program by ear. A second timbre needs a rack authored with an alternative in it, and this capture is written so that adding one is an edit to this list rather than a re-capture.
_dimensions: 9 of the 10 a sustained voice can be judged on. `stereo` is the exclusion and it is measured: the two channels are bit-identical sample for sample, so there is no width to compare against. It is the same exclusion the captured slots of this family already carry.
_dimensions_na: The exclusions as data, since a dimension argued only in prose reads as a gap.

dimensions_na.stereo: the slot renders dual mono: the two channels are bit-identical sample for sample, so the width is zero by construction rather than by voicing

_history: This voice was previously recorded as unusable because its samples were said to stop while the key is still down. Re-measured, they do not: it holds 2.9 dB under its peak at the end of an eight-second gate, and the steepest single 10 ms step anywhere inside the held note is 0.2 dB, which is the instrument's own movement. A sample running out reads quite differently -- the two voices on the neighbouring racks that genuinely do it step 47 and 53 dB in one window and are at the noise floor immediately after.
_identity: Which product this is captured from lives in the untracked sibling `muted_trumpet.local.json`: the plugin's component triple and the slot's preset. Everything here is the method. Re-capturing needs the overlay; scoring, fitting and diagnosing read `reference/muted_trumpet.json` and need nothing.
_slots: Slot identity is measured, never taken from a name or a position, and on this rack it is checkable against the repository's own committed measurements: six of its sixteen slots were captured in an earlier round. Rendered under that capture's own gate at a cell its profile holds, slot 9 returns a peak of -13.58 dBFS against a committed -13.58, which fixes slot n as GM program 47+n. Every slot of this rack near this one was compared against its neighbours at both ends of this grid and at its middle, and all are distinct audio -- the sample sharing that three slots of another rack show outside their instruments' ranges does not happen here.
